You are fixing marketing COPY in the Nxeon repo worktree at /opt/nxeon-wt-pricing (Next.js 15 App Router + Tailwind). Edit ONLY this one file: app/(marketing)/web-hosting/page.tsx. Do NOT touch any other file. Do NOT run any build, `next build`, `prisma generate`, or `prisma db push` — editing only.

SHARED PROMO FACTS (single source of truth):
- ONE promotion site-wide: **First month free** (first month $0, then the regular monthly price forever; capped 1/account + 1/IP). NOT "% off", NOT annual.
- Billing is monthly, prepaid from a wallet. No annual/multi-year terms.
- Shared hosting plans read live from the DB (db.hostingPlan): Starter $2.99, Business $4.99, Pro $8.99 (regular monthly prices). These are correct — DO NOT change prices.

THE PROBLEM: the web-hosting page is the ONLY product page that shows NO promotion at all, while VPS and Business Email both surface the promo. This inconsistency was flagged by the owner. Add first-month-free messaging so hosting has parity.

YOUR TASK in app/(marketing)/web-hosting/page.tsx:
1. Read the file to see how it renders plans (it maps db.hostingPlan and shows money(p.priceCents)).
2. Add a "First month free" promo treatment consistent with the rest of the site — e.g. a small banner near the hero and/or a per-plan line "First month free, then $X/mo". Show the REGULAR price as the headline (do NOT invent a discounted ongoing price — only month one is free).
3. If lib/promotions.ts exports a helper/promo object the other pages use to render the promo (e.g. currentPromo), reuse it here for consistency rather than hardcoding — but if that's awkward, a simple static "First month free" badge is acceptable since there is only one promo. Do NOT edit lib/promotions.ts.
4. Keep the existing layout, the live DB price rendering, and "Free SSL + email + SFTP" copy intact. Additive change — don't redesign.
5. Keep JSX/TS valid; add any needed import.

Read the file first, make the edit, then report: what promo treatment you added and where, and confirm regular prices are unchanged and shown as the headline. Final message is a report to the orchestrator — concise and factual.

NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)

Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.

Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).

Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.

Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.

1	/**
2	 * Promotional pricing — the SINGLE, sitewide "first month free" offer.
3	 *
4	 * There is exactly one promo now (owner decision, 2026-08-11): the customer's
5	 * FIRST TERM is free, then the plan renews at its regular price. This replaced
6	 * three contradictory mechanics that used to run at once — a rotating 15–45%
7	 * intro discount, a fictional "20% off 3-year annual billing" band, and a
8	 * homepage annual toggle — which produced three different live prices for the
9	 * same plan and contradicted the homepage pledge that the sign-up price is the
10	 * renewal price. Under first-month-free that pledge is finally TRUE: you sign up
11	 * free and then renew at exactly the price shown ($X/mo).
12	 *
13	 * It is modelled as a 100%-off-first-term discount so every existing call site
14	 * keeps working untouched:
15	 *   - promoPriceCents(regular) => 0            (the first-term charge is $0)
16	 *   - currentPromo(now).discountPercent === 100
17	 * The "regular" (strikethrough) price is the genuine renewal price. Renewal
18	 * paths (worker/billing.ts, worker/product-renewals.ts, lib/renewal-charge.ts)
19	 * bill plan.priceCents unchanged — never the promo price — so displayed ===
20	 * charged both at sign-up ($0) and at renewal ($X).
21	 *
22	 * Add-ons (dedicated IP, extra disk) are billed at full price at order time;
23	 * the promo only touches the plan portion (see lib/order.ts).
24	 *
25	 * Pure & deterministic: every helper takes `now` as a parameter (kept for API
26	 * compatibility even though the single promo is always-on). Nothing here calls
27	 * Date.now() at module load, so it is safe to import anywhere.
28	 */
29	
30	export type Promo = {
31	  id: string;
32	  /** Full name, e.g. "First month free". */
33	  name: string;
34	  /** Short badge text. */
35	  label: string;
36	  /** Percent off the FIRST-term charge (0–100). 100 = first term free. */
37	  discountPercent: number;
38	  /** True for the sitewide first-month-free offer. */
39	  firstMonthFree: boolean;
40	};
41	
42	/**
43	 * The one and only promo: always on, first term free, then renews at the
44	 * regular price. No countdown, no rotation — nothing to expire, so nothing to
45	 * fake a timer on.
46	 */
47	export const FIRST_MONTH_FREE: Promo = {
48	  id: "first-month-free",
49	  name: "First month free",
50	  label: "First month free",
51	  discountPercent: 100,
52	  firstMonthFree: true,
53	};
54	
55	/**
56	 * The active promo for `now`. There is only one, and it is always on, so this
57	 * always returns it. (Kept taking `now` for call-site compatibility.)
58	 */
59	export function currentPromo(_now: Date): Promo {
60	  return FIRST_MONTH_FREE;
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * The one discount formula: round(regularCents * (1 - discountPercent/100)).
65	 *
66	 * Split out from `promoPriceCents` so proration can price against the percent a
67	 * server's term was ACTUALLY sold at (Server.termPromoPercent) without inventing
68	 * a fake `Promo` object to carry the number — and, crucially, without a second
69	 * copy of this line. Checkout and proration must round identically or an upgrade
70	 * and its mirror-image downgrade stop cancelling.
71	 */
72	export function discountedCents(regularCents: number, discountPercent: number): number {
73	  return Math.round(regularCents * (1 - discountPercent / 100));
74	}
75	
76	/**
77	 * The genuine first-term price for a regular price under `promo`. This exact
78	 * value is what checkout charges for the first term — display it verbatim. Under
79	 * first-month-free (100% off) this is $0.
80	 */
81	export function promoPriceCents(regularCents: number, promo: Promo): number {
82	  return discountedCents(regularCents, promo.discountPercent);
83	}
84	
85	/**
86	 * The DEEPEST discount this platform has ever run. With a single 100%-off promo
87	 * this is 100.
88	 *
89	 * Used as the conservative fallback rate for a server whose sold rate is
90	 * genuinely unrecoverable (lib/proration.ts `resolveTermPromoPercent`). "Assume
91	 * they paid the least we have ever charged" keeps a prorated CREDIT below the
92	 * cash actually collected. Proration prices a DELTA, so at 100% both the upgrade
93	 * charge and the downgrade credit collapse to zero — a revenue concession on an
94	 * unknown-rate row, never a payout.
95	 */
96	export function deepestPromoPercent(): number {
97	  return FIRST_MONTH_FREE.discountPercent;
98	}
99	
100	/**
101	 * Kept for API compatibility. The single promo is always-on and has no honest
102	 * close date, so callers no longer render a countdown; this returns `now` for
103	 * any straggler that still expects a Date.
104	 */
105	export function promoEndsAt(now: Date, _promo: Promo): Date {
106	  return now;
107	}

Done. All edits are in the single target file `/opt/nxeon-wt-pricing/app/(marketing)/web-hosting/page.tsx`.

What I added (additive, reusing the same pattern the Business Email page already uses):

1. Imports: `currentPromo` from `@/lib/promotions` and `PromoBadge` from `@/components/marketing/PromoBadge` — no changes to those files.
2. `const promo = currentPromo(new Date());` in the page component.
3. Plans-section banner: a `PromoBadge` + "First month free — then the price you sign up at is the price you renew at." panel, placed right under the "Simple monthly plans" section title (mirrors the business-email treatment exactly, same classes/gradient).
4. Per-plan treatment: an emerald "First month free" pill above the price, plus a subline "$0 today, then $X/mo. Cancel anytime." under it, using the live DB value `money(p.priceCents)`.

Prices: unchanged. The DB-driven `money(p.priceCents)` remains the headline (still the 3xl bold `/mo` figure — Starter $2.99, Business $4.99, Pro $8.99 as read from `db.hostingPlan`). No discounted ongoing price was invented; only month one is stated as free. Existing layout, live price rendering, and the "Free SSL + email + SFTP" line are all intact. JSX/TS is valid (reused existing typed components and helpers).

Per instructions, I did not run any build or Prisma command, and edited no other file.
